items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on d4 is attacked twice. Which pawn move closes the centre and attacks the knight on c6?

claims.statement: At depth 16 d5 is the engine's first choice.
After d5 a white pawn attacks c6.
The alternative dxe5 scores at least 25 cp worse than d5 (depth 16).

hints: Which pawn can leave the attacked square and hit the knight at the same time?
The pawn moves one square forward and attacks c6 and e6.
The d-pawn advances to d5.
items.explain: The pawn on d5 attacks the knight on c6 and locks the centre: Black's pawn on e5 is now blocked. The alternative dxe5 releases the tension; at depth 16 it scores at least 25 cp worse than d5.

feedback_by_move.d4e5: It trades the centre pawns and the queens come off, which throws away the space advantage that 8.d5 keeps.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on c6 is attacked by the pawn on d5. Which retreat is the main-line move?

claims.statement: At depth 16 Ne7 is the engine's first choice.
...Nd4 scores at least 30 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
...Nb4 scores at least 50 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at which squares the knight can reach and which of them stay near the king side.
One retreat leaves the knight a route to g6 and supports a later ...f5.
The knight goes to e7.
items.explain: From e7 the knight can reach g6 or support the pawn advance on the kingside, and it leaves no piece to be hit again at once. The jumps to b4 and d4 give the knight a square but lose time or the pawn on e5's support; at depth 16 they score clearly worse.

feedback_by_move.c6d4: After Nxd4 exd4 the queen takes the pawn on d4 and Black has lost a pawn.
feedback_by_move.c6b4: The knight is far from the kingside and White can chase it with a3.

feedback_by_move.yes, a pawn: The pawn on d6 simply takes the knight on e5, and White has nothing to take back with.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Ne1. Which knight move clears f6 for the f-pawn and keeps an eye on c5?

claims.statement: At depth 16 Nd7 is the engine's first choice here.
After Nd7 the knight attacks c5.
The alternative ...Nh5 scores at least 30 cp worse (depth 16).

hints: The knight must leave f6 and stay useful.
Which square from f6 also attacks c5?
The knight goes to d7.
items.explain: From d7 the knight attacks c5 and b6 and leaves f6 free for the f-pawn's plan. The jump to h5 puts the knight on the rim, where it has few squares; at depth 16 it scores at least 30 cp worse.

feedback_by_move.f6h5: The knight lands on the edge and White can answer with g3 or Nd3; the f-pawn plan is not helped.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn on f5 attacks the pawn on e4. Which pawn move supports e4 and keeps the centre closed?

claims.statement: At depth 16 f3 is the engine's first choice.
After f3 two white pieces defend e4 (knight c3 and pawn f3).
The alternative exf5 scores at least 60 cp worse (depth 16).

hints: Count attackers and defenders of e4 after Black's move.
You need a second defender or a way to keep the pawn there.
The f-pawn goes to f3.
items.explain: The pawn on f3 becomes a second defender of e4 and holds the centre closed, so ...f5 wins nothing. The capture exf5 gxf5 trades pawns, gives up the pawn that held the closed centre, and scores at least 60 cp worse at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.e4f5: After gxf5 material is level, but White has given up the pawn that held the closed centre, and Black gets a half-open g-file.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just played ...f4. What does Black threaten?

claims.statement: One black piece (the pawn on f4) attacks the bishop on e3.
If White passes, ...fxe3 wins the bishop for nothing.

hints: Which of White's pieces does the new pawn touch?
The pawn on f4 attacks two squares diagonally; one of them holds a white piece.
Black threatens ...fxe3, winning the bishop.
items.explain: The pawn on f4 attacks the bishop on e3, and nothing of White's defends it, so Black threatens to take it for free. The bishop must move or be defended.

items.prompt: White to move after 11...f4. The bishop on e3 is attacked. Which retreat is the main-line move?

claims.statement: At depth 16 Bf2 is the engine's first choice.
One black piece (the rook on a8) defends the pawn on a7.
The grab Bxa7 scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: List the squares the bishop can reach and ask what each one attacks and what attacks it.
One retreat takes a pawn that looks free; check who defends it before you decide.
The bishop goes to f2.
items.explain: On f2 the bishop is safe, defended by the king and the rook, and it still looks toward h4 and the kingside. Grabbing the pawn on a7 fails because the rook on a8 defends it: White loses a bishop for a pawn. At depth 16 it scores at least 300 cp worse.

feedback_by_move.e3a7: The rook on a8 takes the bishop: a bishop for a pawn.
feedback_by_move.e3d2: It is safe, but about 0.7 pawn worse: the bishop on d2 blocks the queen and the plan with b4.
feedback_by_move.e3c1: Too passive: it undoes the development of the bishop.
